name: mab-bernoulli
description: Classical MAB: 10 Bernoulli instances with 10 arms (means uniform in [0.05, 0.95], gap >= 0.05), 2 runs each. Theoretical defaults.

policies.label: UCBV
notes: zeta=1.2 (any zeta > 1 keeps the bound of Theorem 4)

policies.label: UCBMinV1
notes: zeta=1.2 (any zeta > 1 keeps the bound of Theorem 4)

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: Some policies used the **values from their papers**: alpha=1 for UCB1, UCB1Tuned, UCBV and UCBMinV1; c=3 for KLUCB. These values are safe in theory, except for UCB1Tuned: it has **no regret guarantee** (see below). In practice, they often **explore too much**. The regret can then be higher than with tuned values.
notices.todo: Search the best values with param_grid=True. Or set them yourself, e.g. UCB1(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: No regret guarantee
notices.text: UCB1Tuned has **no proven regret bound**: Auer et al. (2002) prove none. Its results can still be good, but nothing bounds its regret.
notices.default: Policies as in their papers: no projection, no buckets, no k-means (n_components=None, n_buckets=None, user_model="shared").
notices.todo: For a regret bound, pick a policy that has one (its docstring says), or turn off its heuristic option.

notices.title: Values with no theoretical choice
notices.text: Some policies kept defaults with **no value from theory**: zeta=1.2 (any zeta > 1 keeps the bound of Theorem 4) for UCBV and UCBMinV1. Other values can give a lower or a higher regret.
notices.default: These values (each policy's docstring explains them).
notices.todo: Search them with param_grid, e.g. param_grid={"zeta": [...]}.

notices.title: Not stored
notices.text: This run **did not store** the per-action estimates and the action of every step. The charts cannot show them.
notices.default: Regret, reward, CPU time and wall time only (track=(), measure_memory=False).

notices.title: Curves stored every 50 steps
notices.text: The curves kept one value every 50 steps. Between two kept steps, the line is **drawn, not measured**. You set log_interval=50.

notices.title: Slower timings
notices.text: Peak memory was measured (measure_memory=True). This made Python code about **5 times slower**. So the CPU times are higher than in a normal run.
